Three Projects, One Process

I built three unrelated things with AI agents.

I extracted every process rule, ritual and check each one used.

This is what recurred.

One person ran all three projects, so nothing here was invented twice over: this is the same hand reaching for the same tool, three times, on three unrelated kinds of work. What is worth reading is which tools it kept reaching for.

126 building blocks — distilled from 212 elements→ One recurring idea about how to work. 23 in all three projects→ A building block that shows up in all three projects. 26 shape-shifters→ A building block that took a different form in different projects: a stated belief in one, a routine step in another, a blocking check in a third.

The three projects the cast

Unrelated products, one owner, one way of working with agents. Each has a ledger page — the full written-up list of that project's process elements, one entry per rule, ritual or check. The numbers above are what happens when you lay all three ledgers side by side.

pairflow

pairflow is a tool for running AI coding agents through a review-gated workflow. The part described here is the ground-up rebuild of its core: one person plus throwaway AI sessions, working from a design model the owner personally approves before any code is written.

Unit of work
one task packet — a self-contained brief a fresh agent builds and closes
Scale
77 process elements catalogued from the core rebuild
open the pairflow ledger →

project-s

project-s (real name withheld — unlaunched product) is not code at all: it is the design corpus for an AI architecture, so its development process is a writing and review process. One person owns every acceptance, while throwaway AI sessions draft, attack and re-review the documents.

Unit of work
one chapter of the corpus, drafted then reviewed until the rounds go quiet
Scale
64 process elements over a documents-only repository
open the project-s ledger →

confpipeline

confpipeline is a research pipeline built by one person with supervised AI agents: every subject gets a lightweight first pass, and only owner-approved cases proceed to in-depth research. The design lives in small owner-gated documents, and scripts generate every index and view.

Unit of work
one build slice — interview, spec, review, delegated build, verification
Scale
71 process elements behind a two-stage research pipeline
open the confpipeline ledger →

One unit of work, start to finish 8 steps

Illustrative compositeAssembled from all three projects, not a transcript of any single real run.

  1. 01 A brief is written that carries everything the work needs, in full — no chat history, no links to go chase.
  2. 02 It goes to a fresh AI session that has never seen the conversation, so anything missing from the brief shows up immediately.
  3. 03 The work is committed, then a second AI model from a different family is pointed at the exact committed files.
  4. 04 Fingerprints are taken before and after the review, so the verdict names precisely which bytes it judged.
  5. 05 Every finding it raises gets exactly one written answer — folded in, narrowed, declined, or deferred — each with a one-line reason.
  6. 06 The author decides each one; the reviewer never edits the document itself.
  7. 07 One command runs the whole battery of machine checks, and any red member means the work is not done.
  8. 08 Then the human — and only the human — accepts it, and the next unit of work starts the same arc over again.

Every step links to the building block it comes from, further down this page.

Owner ratification gate

gateGAT-01
  • pairflowThe contract-draft ratification act — Anchored on the contract-draft act specifically: no packet may anchor to a draft the human has not ratified on named bytes, and re-ratification after a reopen is 'permanently human'.
  • project-sOwner ratification — The general form: the owner personally closes every acceptance on both tracks, recorded in status lines and its own commits; flagged 'un-automatable by definition'.
  • confpipelineOwner ratification — The general form: nothing moves draft-to-accepted, no slice or phase closes, and no gated fold lands on an accepted artifact without the owner's act.
Full description, each project's full text, and evidence

The single identity-bound acceptance act: only the human owner can flip work to accepted, and performing that act deliberately sits outside every machine surface. Machines may verify the paperwork's shape but never substitute for the act.

pairflow The contract-draft ratification act

Anchored on the contract-draft act specifically: no packet may anchor to a draft the human has not ratified on named bytes, and re-ratification after a reopen is 'permanently human'. The lint checks the ratification block's shape and C-row byte-equality, but the act itself sits outside every machine surface. Other never-automated human acts (chapter ratification, draft ratification) are listed inside G10.

project-s Owner ratification

The general form: the owner personally closes every acceptance on both tracks, recorded in status lines and its own commits; flagged 'un-automatable by definition'.

confpipeline Owner ratification

The general form: nothing moves draft-to-accepted, no slice or phase closes, and no gated fold lands on an accepted artifact without the owner's act.

Machine checks that the corpus's cross-reference graph holds: every ID, anchor, or contract reference resolves in its authority file, declared pairings between artifact families are one-to-one, and dangling or duplicate references are hard errors.

pairflow Packet/draft lint + decision record integrity check

Two machine linters: G3 validates packet and draft claim families (machine-block schemas, contract refs resolving to a ratified draft, lane-id completeness, ratified rows byte-equal to git history — its strict modes gate approvals and closes); G7 checks decision record statuses, dangling decision record refs, supersede reciprocity, cycles, index consistency.

project-s Referential-integrity + anchor-integrity + one-to-one name mapping checks

Three sibling functions: INV/ABS/S/DA references must resolve in their authority file (dangling = error, orphan definition = warn); heading anchors globally unique and every link-form citation resolving; question-bank slugs one-to-one with the concept inventory. Grouped as one entry because all three are reference-resolution legs of the same script.

confpipeline The spec-to-skill pairing check

The one-to-one mapping form: every accepted workflow spec has exactly one resolving runbook and vice versa; a runbook without a resolving spec header, duplicates, and stale pending markers all block. Every generated artifact must be byte-identical to what a fresh rebuild produces; a source change cannot land green without regenerating its views. This is what makes 'generated, never hand-maintained' enforceable.

External-arm review gate regime

gateGAT-07
  • pairflowThe two mandatory external-arm gates — On the autonomous path the arm must pass twice — at approve (verdict citing the final hash, zero fold-now findings) and at build close (including the sensitivity pass proving every declared…

  • confpipelineThe external-arm regime — The arm runs automatically at three fixed lifecycle points and otherwise only on owner order; a byte-guard mismatch voids the verdict; semantic findings escalate to the owner…
Full description, each project's full text, and evidence

A pinned, different AI model must sign off at declared points, and its verdict counts only when bound byte-exactly to a committed tree: fingerprints before and after, a hash-citing verdict, and an unavailable arm means a loud stop or an explicit human waiver — never a silent skip.

pairflow The two mandatory external-arm gates

on the autonomous path the arm must pass twice — at approve (verdict citing the final hash, zero fold-now findings) and at build close (including the sensitivity pass proving every declared test able to fail). Unavailable arm = BLOCKER STOP; waive is the human's explicit act per gate.

project-s Arm-mechanics guard: clean tree + byte-guard + hash-citing verdict

the arm may only run on a committed tree, reviewed bytes are hash-guarded before/after, and a verdict that does not cite the basis hashes is no verdict. No script computes any of it.

confpipeline The external-arm regime

the arm runs automatically at three fixed lifecycle points and otherwise only on owner order; a byte-guard mismatch voids the verdict; semantic findings escalate to the owner; an unavailable pin means a loud wait or a recorded owner waiver. The sha256 byte-guard is hand-run — no repo script computes it.

gateGAT-10

pairflow The chapter Definition of Done

confpipeline The Build DoD

Five conditions: master check green with the new guards, tests green, the runbook walked end-to-end on a fictional subject, one-item-one-commit, decision log current — with real-data verification and the slice-close arm following as their own gates.

The recurring unit-of-work cycle

mechanismMEC-03

Full description, each project's full text, and evidence

Every unit of work runs the same fixed multi-stage arc — prepare/spec, review, build/draft, verify, fold back, owner-accept, commit — so the process is a loop over identical cycles rather than a bespoke path per task.

pairflow The packet build loop

The finest grain of the three: a fixed steps-0-to-8 cycle per plan packet (author packet, TDD from declared claims, implement, drift tests, decision record, review, one-commit, audit), with the R-ALIGNED-UP rule folding contradicting decisions up into the plan in the same commit.

project-s The tour per-chapter loop

Per tour chapter: seed quiz questions, draft in three depth tiers, notes-blind fresh-reader test, owner review, accept, commit; the seed-before-draft ordering is practiced but unwritten.

The repo is the institution

Someone patches the symptom downstream, and the design keeps on lying.

The ratified design is the sole truth; divergence routes back through its one change path

gatemechanismprinciplePRC-04
  • pairflowThe two planes must not shear — Model corpus vs implementation: the implementation consumes and never edits; a model bug found during implementation is never silently patched in code.
  • project-sThe model is the truth; narrative is derivative — Model vs tour: a tour sentence contradicting the model is a tour bug unless the owner rules it a model finding, which routes as a backtrack.
  • confpipelineThe divergence stop — Spec vs build: a spec or model bug found mid-build stops the work and returns through the model plane as a gated edit — 'never improvise'.
Full description, each project's full text, and evidence

The design model/spec is the only source of semantic truth. Downstream consumers (code, narrative/tour) never patch it locally: a bug found downstream is a mandatory stop, and the fix returns through the model plane's single sanctioned change path. Pairflow carries this as three separate elements (principle + change-path mechanism + divergence-stop gate); project-s states it as one principle, confpipeline enforces it as one gate.

pairflow The two planes must not shear

Model corpus vs implementation: the implementation consumes and never edits; a model bug found during implementation is never silently patched in code. Gate is the enforcing stop.

A concrete pipeline: edit model sources, rebuild, regenerate the ledger, pass the byte-identical/freshness check, human ratification, re-pin the code mirrors; every model-touching act leaves a process-log reflection. K0-admitted semantics may never enter as direct code edits.

A model bug surfacing during implementation is a mandatory stop, 'NEVER silently patched in code' — it routes through the model plane and returns via the regenerated ledger, user-gated. The one control that can halt a build for a reason no machine surface can see; its downstream half IS machine-enforced (drift trio + freshness).

project-s The model is the truth; narrative is derivative

Model vs tour: a tour sentence contradicting the model is a tour bug unless the owner rules it a model finding, which routes as a backtrack.

Anchored as a principle: the tour simplifies but never becomes a second authority; a tour sentence contradicting the model is a tour bug unless the owner rules it a model finding, which routes back as a backtrack.

The same routing anchored as a principle: a tour statement contradicting the model is a tour bug unless the owner rules it a model finding, which routes as a backtrack into the model. No gate-typed item carries it.

confpipeline The divergence stop

Spec vs build: a spec or model bug found mid-build stops the work and returns through the model plane as a gated edit — 'never improvise'.

Anchored as a gate: a spec or model bug found mid-build stops the work, is fixed in the model plane as a gated edit, and the build resumes from the corrected spec — 'never improvise'.

Code never silently departs from the spec: a spec or model bug found mid-build goes back to the model plane as a gated edit and returns through it; the runbooks mirror it ('never improvise').

Deliberate not-doing is a recorded decision with a revisit trigger

ART-07Append-only in-flight capture logs (friction + decisions) artifact The annoyance you hit mid-task is forgotten by the time you could fix it.

Flat, append-only logs where friction and decisions are captured the moment they occur — deliberately without workflow machinery — and triaged later at a boundary, never fixed mid-flow.

ART-08Incident-distilled rulemaking and its rule registry artifact unclassifiedshape-shifter The same mistake repeats, because the lesson only lived in someone's memory.

Failures are turned into standing rules that carry their provenance — the named incident that bred them — and the rule stock is curated (absorbed, retired) rather than accumulated.

  • pairflow artifact The learned-rule registry row A8 R-<SLUG> table rows with imperative rule + provenance citing the dated log line each was born from; written admission procedure; the registry shrinks and deepens (23 to 16 rows) via absorption at chapter boundaries.

A test form where a declarative fixture (scenario steps or a miniature repo tree) runs through the real machinery and the result is compared exactly against a committed expectation.

The executable procedure layer (runbook or packaged skill) paired to a canonical spec carries only how-to-run mechanics; on any disagreement the canonical docs win, and content the runbook wants beyond the spec is by definition a spec gap. Pairflow adds a validate-before-skillify timing rule.

Adds a graduation rule: a flow starts as template + checklist run by hand and becomes a repo-local skill only after repeated live runs validate the shape (executed once, after 14 live packets); the skill is never promoted globally on a sample size of one.

Anchored as an artifact form: the runbook opens with a bare spec pointer, says only how, and routes any beyond-spec content back as a spec gap through the gated edit.
GAT-02One-command machine check battery gate mechanismshape-shifter Nobody remembers which five checks to run before calling it done.

A single composite entry point runs the project's whole machine-check battery, and any red member means the work is not done. Posture differs: confpipeline makes the composite THE master gate, while pairflow deliberately denies the runner gate status (member gates keep canonical authority) and wires enforcement into hook+CI.

  • pairflow gate mechanism Pre-push hook -> pnpm ci:local / GitHub Actions V3 checks G1 G2 M16 Two enforcement surfaces for the same six-check battery (lint, typecheck, tests, decision record check, coverage lock, packet lint): a pre-push git hook locally and GitHub Actions on main. G1 additionally hides the external arm binary so the external arm can never run inside the machine chokepoint. Grouped as one project entry because the ledger's own text says G2 runs 'the same six v3 bridges'.

Notably NO hook or CI runs it — the process documents say when it must run.
MEC-05Fresh-context delegated build mechanism Whoever builds it fills the gaps from a conversation nobody else heard.

The actual build work is handed to a fresh sub-agent that receives only self-contained repo artifacts, never chat context — decorrelating author from builder and doubling as the spec's self-containment test.

  • pairflow mechanism Fresh-context delegated build (the conductor architecture) with the entry-mode trust dial M7 The conductor keeps orchestration, verification chain, and the commit boundary while a subagent fed the self-contained packet executes the build; the user's opening prompt sets the autonomy mode (per-packet / review-stop / standing chapter mode), and a ratified workflow's subagents count as user-requested.
  • confpipeline mechanism Repo-bound delegated build M5 Every major build step runs in a fresh-context subagent fed only repo artifacts; the builder's final report must map every deterministic-marked spec step to its implementing script.
MEC-11Real-substrate verification at close mechanism It works on the test data and falls over on the real thing.

Before a unit of work closes, the shipped thing is exercised against the real environment or real data it will live with — catching the 'reality is not what we assumed' failure class that internal test harnesses structurally miss — and misses fold back through the normal channels.

  • pairflow mechanism Dogfooding runs M10 Shipped operator tooling is driven by hand or script against real tmux, worktrees, and gate spawns before chapter close; findings land as process-log lines; waivable only by the user's explicit recorded act; includes a real-LLM basic-workflow run from ch9 on.
  • confpipeline mechanism Real-data verification with gated fold-back M8 After DoD the slice runs on real subjects; the owner judges outputs against frozen exemplars or known-correct reference outcomes, and misses fold back into the model as ordinary gated edits — also where spec-time deferred-to-build findings are checked.
MEC-13Big-change ritual: enumerate, review, then execute mechanism artifactshape-shifter A huge change lands in one go, and nobody could really review it.

A change too large for normal in-place editing is first materialized as an enumerated surface (claim rows or a standalone design memo), reviewed — including by the external arm — and ratified as a whole, then executed to satisfy exactly those rows; the enumeration file remains the audit record.

  • pairflow mechanism The claim-enumeration audit ritual for authority rewrites M13 Before rewriting a surface agents execute, every claim the new text will make is enumerated as rows, swept, and arm-reviewed; the change is written to satisfy exactly those rows. Before rewriting agent-executed surfaces, every claim the new text will make is enumerated as rows, swept, and arm-reviewed; the change satisfies exactly those rows and the row file stays as the post-landing audit record.
  • confpipeline mechanism artifact Redesign design-doc with gated-edit derivation list M16 A19 A too-large change is written as a self-contained design document, arm-reviewed at first draft, and after ratification derives an enumerated list of ordinary gated edits while remaining as the rationale record. A numbered-section proposal (basis, measured problem, target structure, gated-edit derivation list, verification plan) carried through its own review gate; one instance, form named nowhere else (practiced, not recorded).
PRC-13A rule nothing enforces is a planning gap principle A rule nobody can check quietly stops being followed by anyone.

Every binding rule must map to a machine check, test, or recorded decision with a verification clause; unenforced prose rules are assumed to erode and are treated as holes, not rules.

  • pairflow principle A rule without an enforcement surface is a planning gap, and a decision record without a verification clause is prose P5 Every binding IC-* constraint must map to a test, check, or decision record, and every decision record's Verification section is mandatory.
  • confpipeline principle Checks enforce what prose declares P3 Driven by the observation that 'rules that no check enforces erode'; a red check means the work is not done — qualified by build-only-what-the-next-phase-consumes.
PRC-14Evidence over claims; a check must be proven able to fail principle mechanism gateshape-shifter A green check that could never turn red proves absolutely nothing.

A completeness or quality claim counts only with its measurement attached, and a test or guard counts only once demonstrated able to go red when the thing it protects is broken — 'a guard no test can fail is decoration'. Pairflow splits this into principle + sabotage-receipt mechanism + gates-selftest gate; confpipeline mandates a negative-test layer inside its test-suite gate.

  • pairflow principle mechanism gate Evidence over claims; "driven" means able to fail P7 M11 G18 Sweep claims need untruncated measurement output ('enumeration from memory is not a measurement'); test lanes must be proven able to fail — operationalized by the receipt-backed mutation probes. Runtime form: a probe runner does byte-copy backup → mutate → run → verified restore and emits a receipt JSON (command, exit code, suite_red, restore_verified) cited by the packet's build record; a green-baseline gate aborts probes against an already-red suite. Sibling rule: substrate claims are probed, not presumed. The four Python checker gates chain --selftest before every run: throwaway fixtures prove each failure dimension actually goes red plus one green control proving the reds are not ambient; a decayed selftest turns the main CI gates red. The decision record bridge carries no selftest (recorded gap).
  • confpipeline gate The test suite with mandated layers G6 The able-to-fail half as a mandated test layer: a negative test per invariant guard, written from the declared prohibition — 'a guard no test can fail is decoration'. Anchored as a gate: the test minimum mandates a negative test per invariant guard written from the declared prohibition ('a guard no test can fail is decoration'), plus a golden-run fixture and freshness layers. The test-suite gate whose distinctive mandate is the same doctrine: a negative test per invariant guard written from the declared prohibition, plus one golden-run fixture through the full write path and freshness guards; 672 tests green at head.
PRC-15Autonomy ends at the judgment boundary principle The automation guesses at the one decision it should have handed you.

An AI loop may run unattended exactly as far as machines can verify its results; the moment a decision it cannot safely make appears, it stops and hands the human a proposal instead of guessing.

  • pairflow principle Autonomy is proportional to contract density; the loop stops exactly where a new semantic decision is needed P3 Design-time form: machine-checkable acceptance is necessary (not sufficient — first-of-a-kind always goes to the human), ratification is explicit and never delegated, and a separate loop-economics stop family exists.
  • confpipeline principle Never a guess: unsafe judgments escalate P13 Runtime form: a judgment the LLM cannot make safely becomes an owner proposal, never a guess, and unknowns stay recorded as unknown; deliberately unratified as a rule, practiced today.
PRC-16Capture, don't fix principle mechanismshape-shifter You stop to fix a small annoyance and lose the thread entirely.

Friction and process observations get one appended log line the moment they occur; nothing is fixed mid-flow unless blocking, and every captured line receives an explicit verdict in one batch at the next unit boundary (chapter / slice close). Pairflow states the principle and runs the loop; confpipeline carries the loop as a mechanism.

  • pairflow principle mechanism Capture, don't fix: the process changes only at chapter boundaries, and rule retirement has equal standing with addition P9 M6 Adds two pairflow-specific extensions: rule retirement weighs equally with addition (backed by per-rule catch tallies), and the two lawful doors for mid-chapter edits (blocking clause, ratified exception). Append-only process log; at each chapter boundary every new line gets a verdict (gate / rule / README edit / WATCH / non-issue), a per-rule catch tally feeds rule retirement, and the boundary also audits the autonomy machinery and may move the arm pin.
  • confpipeline mechanism Capture-don't-fix friction loop M7 The same named concept as a mechanism: one appended line per friction the moment it occurs, nothing fixed mid-flow unless blocking, everything dispositioned at slice close. Mid-build frictions get one appended line; every line is dispositioned at slice close.
PRC-21The threat model, stated once principle unclassifiedshape-shifter You cannot tell which worries are in scope, so every objection wins.

An explicit one-place statement of what the process defends against — one owner plus supervised, review-gated agents on a single repo, git as the audit trail — and explicitly not against. It bounds every gate's proportionality and grounds declining out-of-scope findings. Near-verbatim wording match between the two projects that have it.

  • pairflow principle The threat model, stated once P15 Defends against agent drift and sloppiness (silent edits, unresolved references, boundary escapes), explicitly never against adversarial history forgery; grounds the routine 'declined: out of threat model' disposition. Gates defend one operator plus review-gated agents against drift and sloppiness, deliberately never against adversarial history forgery; grounds the routine 'declined: out of threat model' disposition.
  • confpipeline unclassified The stated threat model U2 'A single curator plus supervised agents on one repo; git is the audit trail' — the scoping assumption that parameterizes the proportionality gate and P8's earns-its-place judgment. 'A single curator plus supervised agents on one repo; git is the audit trail' — parameterizes the proportionality gate and the every-rule-earns-its-place judgment.

Generated, never hand-maintained viewsART-03universalA3A14A11 P10+1
Registries, indexes, and rendered views are produced by scripts, carry a do-not-edit banner, and are byte-compared against a fresh regeneration so they can never silently go stale; hand-maintained lists are assumed to rot. Confpipeline also states this as an explicit principle.
External-review run evidence: pin + prompt + verdict + byte-guard recordART-12universalA12A17A6
The evidence trail of every external-model review run: which model was pinned, what exact bytes were reviewed (guarded by fingerprints), and the verbatim prompt and verdict — so a verdict is auditable or it does not count.
Declared-inventory-to-realization traceability mapART-17universalA17A8G15
A complete mapping from a declared inventory (model units, design-note items, deterministic spec steps) to where each is realized, under a closure rule: no orphans, nothing silently dropped. In confpipeline the map is a builder duty at delegation close rather than a standing file.
Per-document authority status + review bookkeeping surfaceART-19universalP14A2A5
Governed documents open with a declared authority status (draft/ratified/accepted, ideally naming the conferring act), and the review bookkeeping (basis, rounds, findings, dispositions, acceptance) lives on a defined per-document surface kept out of the semantic reading path.
Owner ratification gateGAT-01universalG9G11G8
The single identity-bound acceptance act: only the human owner can flip work to accepted, and performing that act deliberately sits outside every machine surface. Machines may verify the paperwork's shape but never substitute for the act.
Cross-reference and pairing integrity checksGAT-03universalG3 G7+1G1 G2 G4+2G4
Machine checks that the corpus's cross-reference graph holds: every ID, anchor, or contract reference resolves in its authority file, declared pairings between artifact families are one-to-one, and dangling or duplicate references are hard errors.
Generated-surface freshness / reproducibility checkGAT-05universalG8G6G5
Every generated artifact must be byte-identical to what a fresh rebuild produces; a source change cannot land green without regenerating its views. This is what makes 'generated, never hand-maintained' enforceable.
External-arm review gate regimeGAT-07universalG11G14G9
A pinned, different AI model must sign off at declared points, and its verdict counts only when bound byte-exactly to a committed tree: fingerprints before and after, a hash-citing verdict, and an unavailable arm means a loud stop or an explicit human waiver — never a silent skip.
Multi-leg unit-of-work close checklist (Definition of Done)GAT-10universalG12G10G11
The project's main unit of work (chapter, level, build slice) closes only when a declared multi-leg checklist holds in full, regardless of how finished the content looks — composing machine gates with judgment legs.
External pinned different-model review armMEC-01universalM5M1M4
A second, different AI model family — pinned to an exact version — reviews the exact committed bytes of an artifact under a byte-guard (hashes before/after), producing a verdict that cites its basis; the run's provenance is recorded.
Typed finding-disposition triageMEC-02universalM17M2M3
Every finding any reviewer raises gets exactly one explicit recorded verdict from a closed token set with a one-line reason; nothing is silently absorbed or dropped.
The recurring unit-of-work cycleMEC-03universalM2M8M2
Every unit of work runs the same fixed multi-stage arc — prepare/spec, review, build/draft, verify, fold back, owner-accept, commit — so the process is a loop over identical cycles rather than a bespoke path per task.
The repo is the institutionPRC-01universalP8P1P1
All knowledge an ephemeral AI session needs lives in full on repository surfaces; no session, machine, or assistant memory is ever an authority.
One authority per factPRC-02universalP4P2P4
Every fact and durable decision has exactly one owning artifact, so copies can never silently drift or redefine each other.

The design model/spec is the only source of semantic truth. Pairflow carries this as three separate elements (principle + change-path mechanism + divergence-stop gate); project-s states it as one principle, confpipeline enforces it as one gate.

Capability grows in small coherent increments, and the growth path doubles as a test of the design: if a new capability slots in as a small branch, the abstraction holds; if it forces a tear-up, the earlier model was wrong.

Validation instruments are deliberately deprived of the inputs that would let them pattern-match: the test reader is kept from the notes and pass markers, and questions are unanswerable by echoing the artifact's wording.

The corpus exists first to enable good conversations and an honest size/effort estimate; it counts as an implementation spec only where actually validated, with the MVP cut carried as a column, not a retro.

Design documents are written so they can later serve directly as the running system's configuration, making ID discipline and machine checks pay twice — once at design time, once in production.

The running system never contacts an outside person on its own: every outgoing item needs per-item human approval, no autonomous outbound flow exists, and decision-requiring review findings escalate to the owner.

Which AI model runs a step is per-step configuration, never baked into the workflow, so every step stays swappable to a different or cheaper model later.

How this page was made

The short version, because the method is part of the claim.

  1. Mined. AI agents read the three repositories end to end — commits, working session logs, the documents each project produced — and wrote up every process rule, ritual, artifact and check they found as a named element. That is three ledgers, 212 elements.
  2. Cross-mapped. Semantic matchers, one per element family, compared the three ledgers element by element; a reconciliation pass merged the overlaps so every element has exactly one home. 212 elements became 126 blocks.
  3. Generated. This page is built from those files by a script — no hand-typed HTML — and a freshness check byte-compares it against a fresh rebuild, so it cannot quietly drift away from the data behind it.

Generated views that are byte-compared against a fresh rebuild are themselves one of the 23 universal blocks — Generated, never hand-maintained views. This site is an instance of the process it documents.

Two honest limits. One person ran all three projects, so what recurs here is the same hand reaching for the same tool, not three independent inventions. And universal / pair / unique follows what the ledgers recorded, not what happened: a project can genuinely practice a block that nobody ever wrote down, and it will look absent here.
